review_candidates.title: Program Manager - Housing Stability
review_candidates.description: Agate is seeking two Housing Stability Program Managers to provides leadership, supervision, and program oversight for Agate's resident services at assigned Minneapolis Public Housing Authority (MPHA) Asset Management Projects (AMPs) and properties in the South or North Team service area. The position supports a consistent, housing-focused approach to resident engagement, case management, eviction prevention, resource coordination, and housing stability across properties serving varied resident populations. The Program Manager supervises assigned Case Managers and other designated Team staff, partners closely with MPHA regional and onsite property management teams, and ensures that resident services align with contract requirements, agency practices, and the needs of each community. The role includes scheduled resident-facing presence, staff coaching and case consultation, and coordination with Agate's specialized crisis, targeted intervention, and benefits staff when residents need additional support. This is an in-office position, with flexibility for occasional remote work or adjustments to daily schedule as operational needs allow. Core working hours fall between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., with flexibility in start and end times. Compensation: $70,000__________________________________________________________________________________ Why Work at Agate Housing and Services? At Agate Housing and Services, we believe everyone deserves a safe place to call home, and we are passionate about making that a reality. What makes Agate special is not just the work we do, but the people who do it. Our team is made up of compassionate, dedicated, and driven individuals who show up every day with a shared commitment to making a meaningful difference in the lives of others. We foster a workplace where people support one another, bring new ideas forward, embrace challenges, and take pride in the impact of their work. When you join Agate, you become part of a team that is bigger than any one person, united by a mission to end homelessness and relieve hunger through action and advocacy. If you are looking for meaningful work, great people, and the opportunity to make a lasting difference in your community, we would love to have you be part of Agate! Benefit OverviewPaid Holidays: Agate provides paid holidays, including New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day, plus additional floating holidays. Full-time employees receive up to 88 hours of holiday pay annually, prorated for part-time employees and employees who start during the year. Most agency operations are closed on fixed holidays.See Agate's career page for more information about our benefit plans. Agate offers health insurance through Medica, with traditional and high-deductible plans available across three popular networks, including M Health Fairview and HealthPartners, among others. Agate pays 100% of dental and life insurance premiums and contributes 1.5% of each employee's salary to their retirement account, even if the employee does not contribute. Position Responsibilities: Provide day-to-day supervision, leadership, coaching, and performance support to assigned MPHA Team staff; set clear expectations for resident engagement, housing stabilization, responsiveness, and documentation. Conduct regular individual supervision, team meetings, case consultation, and professional development activities that promote consistent, high-quality services and staff accountability. Oversee service delivery across assigned AMPs and properties, adjusting staff priorities and resident engagement approaches to the needs of senior and disability housing, family housing, mixed-population communities, and other assigned properties. Maintain active, collaborative relationships with MPHA regional and onsite property management teams; establish clear communication, referral, escalation, and follow-up practices. Support staff in early identification of housing stability concerns, including lease compliance, rent or income changes, resident conflict, and barriers to accessing services; coordinate prevention-oriented responses and follow-through. Maintain scheduled resident-facing hours at assigned properties through outreach, resident meetings, service coordination, or direct support appropriate to the managerial role. Provide case consultation and assist staff with complex resident needs, conflicts, and situations requiring coordinated involvement of property management, specialized Agate staff, or community providers. Coordinate with the LICSW Provider and Crisis & Float Team on urgent resident concerns, targeted interventions, temporary coverage, and transitions back to assigned AMP Case Managers. Build working relationships with resident leaders and relevant community organizations, and incorporate resident feedback into service planning and continuous improvement. Monitor workload, scheduling, onsite coverage, staff availability, and cross-coverage needs; identify gaps and communicate staffing or service adjustments to the Director. Review case management documentation and service data for accuracy, timeliness, and quality; provide staff feedback and corrective coaching when needed. Monitor service outcomes, contract deliverables, and program reporting; help prepare timely and accurate information for leadership, MPHA, and funder reporting as assigned. Support budget stewardship, staffing plans, and responsible use of program resources in coordination with the Director, Finance, and other agency partners. Ensure assigned services follow applicable federal, state, local, agency, and MPHA contractual requirements and maintain appropriate confidentiality and professional boundaries. Participate in program planning, implementation, evaluation, and ongoing refinement of the MPHA resident services model; identify opportunities to strengthen housing-focused, accessible services. Represent Agate in MPHA operational meetings, resident service discussions, and community partnership meetings as assigned; elevate significant issues and decisions to the Director. Travel to assigned MPHA properties and community service locations, including resident-facing visits when scheduled or appropriate. Perform other related duties as assigned. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Human Services, Psychology, Sociology, Public Administration, or a related field; or a minimum of three years of relevant professional experience in case management, housing stabilization, resident services, or related human services. Minimum two years of experience managing human services or housing programs and supervising direct service staff. Demonstrated ability to lead and support staff through clear expectations, respectful coaching, case consultation, accountability, and performance management. Experience working with individuals and families facing housing instability or complex service needs, using trauma-informed, person-centered, and strengths-based approaches. Ability to oversee multiple areas of program operations, including service quality, staff supervision, program evaluation, contract compliance, and resource oversight. Strong relationship-building, communication, conflict-resolution, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Ability to work collaboratively with MPHA property management, residents, community partners, agency leadership, and interdisciplinary service teams. Ability to review documentation and program data for completeness and quality, manage competing priorities, and use information to support service coordination and program oversight. Proficiency with Microsoft Office products and ability to learn required case management and reporting systems. Ability to accompany staff on home visits and provide direct resident support at assigned MPHA properties as needed. Must possess a valid Minnesota driver's license, have access to a safe and reliable insured vehicle, and meet applicable driving. Have a valid Driver's License and access to a safe and reliable vehicle. This position requires use of your own personal vehicle and will require insurance liability coverage of at least one hundred thousand dollars per person and three hundred thousand dollars per occurrence and must have a valid Driver's License and pass a driving record review. Preferred Qualifications: Experience working in public housing, subsidized housing, supportive housing, or other community-based housing programs. Familiarity with Minneapolis Public Housing Authority (MPHA) operations, public housing lease requirements, and resident support services. Experience implementing new programs, leading service transitions, or supporting organizational change. Experience coordinating eviction prevention, housing loss prevention planning, and specialized interventions for residents with complex service needs. Experience using program data, service outcomes, and quality assurance processes to improve service delivery and staff performance. Familiarity with Minneapolis and Hennepin County housing, benefits, behavioral health, aging, disability, and community support resources. Knowledge of Housing First and Harm Reduction principles. Master's degree in Social Work, Human Services, Public Administration, or a related field. Minnesota social work licensure (LSW, LGSW, LISW, or LICSW). Fluency in languages used by residents, including Spanish, Amharic, Oromo, Somali, or American Sign Language (ASL). Ways to ApplyWe want to make applying for a position at Agate as easy as possible. You can apply using any of the following methods: Indeed: Apply directly through Indeed. This is often the easiest option if you already have an Indeed account. Minnesota Council of Nonprofits: Apply through the Minnesota Council of Nonprofits job board. This is often the easiest option if you already have an account. Agate Website: Apply through the Agate website using our iSolved application platform. By Email: You can also apply by email at hiring@agatemn.org. Simply send us your resume and an email letting us know which position you are applying for and a little about why you are interested in the position and working at Agate. You do not need to complete an online application when applying by email. We welcome applications through any of these methods and look forward to learning more about you!

This career professional is Compassion's primary liaison to the local church and is responsible for strengthening local ownership, capacity and resources of local church partners to minister to children and youth in their own context. As the primary liaison, this facilitator is responsible for developing relationships with church partners and denominational leaders that are characterized by mutual respect, trust, and service that builds up church ministry. He or she is accountable for managing partner relationships through the Partner Management core process, for improving achievement of church outcomes, and for bringing a developmental mindset to all other aspects of the partnership, including mobilizing staff and other resources to support the church. At this career level, the incumbent generally conducts projects independently or participates as a team member for major, complex, or international initiatives. He or she may coach and oversee the work of other facilitators. Responsibilities Acts as an advocate to raise the awareness of the needs of children. Understands Christ’s mandate to protect children. Commits to and prioritizes child protection considerations in all decision-making, tasks and activities across the ministry. Abides by all behavioral expectations in Compassion’s Statement of Commitment to Child Protection and Code of Conduct. Reports any concerns of abuse, neglect or exploitation of children through Compassion’s internal reporting process and appropriately supports responses to incidents if they occur. Demonstrates a personal commitment to serve, respect, and empower the church according to principles outlined in Compassion’s ministry philosophies. Church Maturation - Strengthens church ownership and capacity through a developmental mindset and the Partnership Management core process. Facilitates partnerships with church leaders to collaboratively reflect on youth and church outcomes and plan for how to best grow in capacity and maturity. Facilitates the development and implementation of church owned strategies that build on each church's strengths to engage participation of parents and caregivers, children and youth in all aspects of the ministry, including program design, local resource mobilization, decision making, etc. Supports churches as they actively identify and engage the change makers who influence change in children and youth, such as parents, schools, peers, etc. Actively facilitates and engages church leadership involvement in the broader community as an agent of social transformation that promotes child development and child protection Works with pastors, other church leaders and church staff to identify capacity development needs. Serves as Compassion’s key liaison with church partners by mobilizing and coaching other Church Facing Team (CFT) members and financial resources in ways that are consistent with a developmental mindset and the Partnership Principles Builds church and cluster capacity for local resource mobilization and sharing of resources among nearby churches. Partners with churches to equip them to identify and mobilize local resources, services and relationships, as well as develop plans to help maximize their own resources to support the ministry to children and youth. Supports the formation and strengthening of strategic relationships and alliances at the cluster or community level to further the ministry impact of partner churches. Program Cycle – Provides support and guidance to the church partner throughout all phases of the Program Cycle Needs Assessment – Mobilizes CFT members to compile and organize information to inform the church partners about the needs of children and youth they serve. Facilitates the church partner in gathering local information about child and youth needs, and synthesizing local data with external data. Planning - Facilitates church partner led planning of their Child and Youth (CY) ministry. Supports the church partner to develop an effective multi-year strategic plan by assisting the church partner to identify and prioritize CY needs as well as select interventions that will address the prioritized needs and challenges. Builds the capacity of the local church leadership to invite greater participation of other church ministry leaders, parents/caregivers, youth, community leaders, and other key stakeholders in identifying needs, planning and implementing CY interventions. Supports the church to develop an annual plan and budget to implement customized program interventions. Implementation – Builds the capacity of church partners, with support from other CFT members, to carry out their chosen interventions and monitor progress toward successful implementation. Evaluation – Facilitates the church partner, with support from other CFT members, through the facilitation of a learning and reflection process on effectiveness of the interventions to inform planning in the next cycle. Builds church capacity for learning and reflection. Coordination of CFT - Coordinates Church Facing Team (CFT) support to each church partner. Through the Facilitation Workplan, sets goals and priorities for how the CFT will support each church partner based on the church’s level of ownership, capacity and resources (maturity), the local context, needs identified by CFT members, local church and denominational priorities and National Office priorities. Creates Facilitation Workplans that are highly strategic and lead to greater effectiveness by targeting each church's individual needs. Facilitates a shared understanding among CFT members of the church’s needs. Reviews reports and support documentation from CFT members, as well as perspectives from the church partner to gain understanding of the church’s unique needs and challenges and mobilize appropriate support for the church partner. Documents, alongside all other CFT members, the support they provide to the church partners and follows up on issues identified. Cluster operations - Oversees a more complex cluster of churches while demonstrating responsiveness to the local context and needs of each individual church within the cluster. Encourages, facilitates and leverages cluster level activities and resources. Proactively seeks to foster relationships and connection within the cluster. Provides opportunities for development of cluster-based collaboration and initiatives between local churches for the purpose of improving ministry to children, peer-to-peer learning, and addressing other needs in the families and the community. Ensures the timely renewal of the partnership agreement between Compassion and the Church partner. Child Protection - Deepens church partner ownership of child protection standards. Facilitates development of church owned and contextualized child protection practices. La personne recrutée participera à la sélection, la production et la caractérisation de protéines artificielles reconnaissant spécifiquement des protéines virales d’intérêt, ainsi qu’à leur intégration dans des dispositifs de détection rapide de type lateral flow assay (LFA). L'Activité Sélectionner, par phage display, des protéines artificielles présentant une affinité et une spécificité adaptées vis-à-vis de protéines virales d’intérêt ; Produire et caractériser les protéines sélectionnées ; Évaluer leurs propriétés de reconnaissance moléculaire et leur potentiel pour la détection des virus ; Mettre en œuvre des stratégies de greffage ou d’immobilisation de ces protéines sur des plateformes permettant l’amplification du signal de détection ; Participer au développement et à l’optimisation de tests rapides de type LFA ; Caractériser les performances des systèmes développés, notamment en termes de sensibilité, spécificité et stabilité ; Analyser et interpréter les résultats expérimentaux ; Contribuer à la présentation et à la valorisation des résultats au sein du consortium INSTEAD et de l’I2BC. Votre Profil Compétences Le ou la candidat(e) devra être idéalement titulaire d’un Master ou d’un diplôme d’ingénieur en biochimie, biotechnologies, biologie moléculaire, microbiologie ou dans un domaine connexe. Une expérience pratique ou des connaissances dans plusieurs des domaines suivants seront particulièrement appréciées : Biologie moléculaire et biochimie (clonage moléculaire et construction de plasmides, culture de microorganismes ; expression et purification de protéines recombinantes) ; Phage display (compétence souhaitée) ; Caractérisation des interactions protéines-protéines. Au-delà des compétences techniques, nous recherchons une personne curieuse, rigoureuse, autonome et motivée par le développement de nouvelles technologies de diagnostic. Une aptitude à travailler en équipe et à interagir dans un environnement scientifique multidisciplinaire sera également appréciée. Votre Environnement de Travail La personne recrutée intégrera l’I2BC et travaillera conjointement avec les équipes Modélisation et Ingénierie des Protéines (MIP- https://www.i2bc.paris-saclay.fr/protein-engineering-and-modeling/ ) et Virologie Bactérienne (https://www.i2bc.paris-saclay.fr/bacterial-virology/ ). L'Institut de Biologie Intégrative de la Cellule (I2BC) situé à Gif-sur-Yvette est une grande unité mixte de recherche CNRS, CEA et Université Paris-Saclay. L'unité a un effectif moyen de près de 650 personnes réparties entre 5 départements scientifiques, 60 équipes de recherche, diverses plateformes technologiques de haut niveau et des services support et soutien (http://www.i2bc.paris-saclay.fr/). Contexte scientifique Les arbovirus West Nile virus (WNV) et Usutu virus (USUV) sont des virus transmis par les moustiques, dont le cycle implique notamment les oiseaux. Leur circulation et leur implantation progressive en Europe constituent une menace croissante pour la santé publique, notamment en France. Le projet INSTEAD – « INnovative and integrated STrategies to EArly mitigate the risk of West Nile Virus and Usutu virus Diseases in France », financé dans le cadre du PEPR PREZODE (2025–2028), vise à améliorer la prévention, la surveillance et la détection précoce de ces arbovirus. Réunissant 17 laboratoires français ainsi que plusieurs partenaires locaux et nationaux, le projet s’inscrit dans une approche intégrée « One Health », prenant en compte les dimensions, humaine, animale et environnementale. INSTEAD a Notamment Pour Objectifs De Développer des méthodes innovantes permettant la détection précoce du WNV et de l’USUV chez les moustiques, les animaux et dans l’environnement ; Mettre en place un système de surveillance intégré, aux échelles locale et nationale, afin de renforcer la préparation face à l’émergence de ces risques infectieux. Dans ce cadre, les équipes Modélisation et Ingénierie des Protéines (MIP) et Virologie Bactérienne de l’Institut de biologie intégrative de la cellule (I2BC) ont pour objectif de développer de nouvelles stratégies de bio-détection basées sur des protéines artificielles capables de reconnaître spécifiquement des cibles virales. Elles cherchent également à développer des stratégies d’affichage de ces protéines sur des plateformes permettant l’amplification du signal de détection. Ces approches seront utilisées pour concevoir et optimiser des tests rapides de type lateral flow assay (LFA). Ce poste offre l’opportunité de participer au développement d’une technologie innovante de détection rapide, avec une finalité directement liée à la surveillance et à la prévention des maladies infectieuses émergentes.
